owner.occupation: Chef running community cooking classes at a church hall

world.bio: I'm Marama, forty-three, an ex-restaurant chef in Auckland who now runs low-cost cooking classes from a church hall kitchen in Mt Albert. I used to run a busy kitchen in Ponsonby, burned out, and found that teaching ordinary people to make dinner from a $20 budget is the best thing I've done. I refuse to use the word 'easy' in any of my recipes. I coach my son's waka ama team, grow chillies on a tiny balcony, and study te reo Māori at night school.
skills_assets: Twenty years in professional kitchens: sous-chef, head chef, and menu development
A church hall kitchen in Mt Albert with six induction hobs, two ovens and a large prep table, available on weeknights
Community cooking classes: Tuesday 'Cooking for One', Thursday 'Blokes Cook', Saturday 'Kids & Parents'
A small grant from a local board covering hall hire and ingredients, with conditions on attendance
A recipe booklet of 40 budget dishes she self-printed
Strong ties to local butchers, greengrocers and a community garden
Level 2 te reo Māori, working towards level 3

projects.name: Blokes Cook
projects.text: Thursday evenings. Started with fourteen men, many of them recently widowed or divorced or retrenched, who had never made a white sauce. We cook together, we eat together, and nobody is allowed to say 'it's only pasta'. Lately numbers have dropped to six regulars. The hall grant requires eight regulars to continue. There is a real chance the grant is withdrawn at the end of the quarter.

projects.name: Saturday Kids & Parents
projects.text: About twelve kids and eight parents. This one runs itself.

notes.text: Thursday class. Six men this week: Mick, Tane, Wiremu, Dave, Sione, and old George who hasn't missed a class in a year. We made a lamb shoulder with white beans. Dave burned the garlic and said sorry about eight times. I said burn is a flavour. He laughed. Everyone ate. Nobody left early.
Board member Susan emailed: attendance numbers are in, six regulars for Thursdays. 'We will need to see eight or the grant can't be justified.' It's polite. It's still a guillotine.

Talked to George after class. He told me about his wife, six months gone, and how he'd never cooked until this class. 'It's the only evening I don't feel alone,' he said. I put the lid on a pot to hide my face.
Tried to recruit more men. Put a flyer on the noticeboard at the Mt Albert pools. Spoke to the barber next door. He said, 'blokes don't do cooking classes.' I said, 'they do if you feed them.'
Son Hemi's waka ama training. Fourteen teenage paddlers in the harbour at dawn. I stood on the shore with a flask and a stopwatch, and thought: community happens when you show up. Even in the cold.
Chilli seedlings on the balcony have finally germinated, three Scotch Bonnets and some Thai. Hemi watered them with a measuring jug and a serious face.
Te reo class tonight. Learned 'Kei te pēhea koe?' I said 'Kei te ngenge au,' I'm tired. The teacher said that's honest. I'm trying.
Called the community garden to ask for a donation of silverbeet. They gave me a box. The woman said, 'Your Thursday class makes the best soup.' I didn't tell her about the grant.

George brought his late wife's recipe card to class. 'Can you show me how to make this?' It was a steak-and-kidney pie. We made it together. He cried a bit. So did I, though I pretended it was onions.

messages.text:
Susan: The numbers are low, Marama.
Me: I know. We're doing outreach.
Susan: We need eight regulars by quarter end.
Me: Understood.

George: I'll bring a friend next week.
Me: Please do.
George: He doesn't cook.
Me: Perfect.

Hemi: Mum, can we have your lamb for dinner?
Me: It's a class recipe.
Hemi: I'll be your best taster.
Me: Deal.

Jim: I'm telling every bloke who comes in.
Me: Tell them there's free pie.
Jim: There's pie?
Me: There will be.

relations.about: Eighty-year-old widower, never missed a class.
Barber next door, willing to help.

constraints: Thursday evenings only; weekends reserved for family
Budget is tight; ingredients must stay under $20 per person
Does not cook anything labelled 'easy' or 'quick'
Will not turn the class into a profit-making venture
sensitive: Worried the class closes and George loses his only evening out
Quietly doubts whether she is doing enough
